label: Tooltip
title: Tooltip
summary: Use a Tooltip to explain a term or icon in a short line that opens from an info button and closes with the next press.

anatomy.title: A trigger, then a bubble over the page
anatomy.description: Only the trigger sits in the page. Pressing it opens a near-black bubble 12 px away, with 8 px corners, 12 × 8 px of padding, white 14 px text that wraps at 280 px, and a 16 × 8 px arrow pointing at the trigger. React Native draws the bubble over the page, so this diagram can't frame it; press the trigger to see it.
blocks: Yours: an info IconButton passed with asChild. Pressing it opens or closes the bubble.
The word it explains. Keep it visible: the bubble only adds detail.

configuration.title: Side and alignment
configuration.description: Placement picks the side, top by default, and can line the bubble up with the trigger's start or end edge instead of its centre. When the bubble doesn't fit on that side it flips to the opposite one, and beside the trigger with no room either way it moves above or below. It always stays 8 px inside the screen.
blocks: The default: the bubble sits above, its arrow pointing down at the trigger.
For triggers near the top of the screen, where there's no room above.
The bubble's start edge lines up with the trigger's; the arrow still points at it.
Next to the trigger, for a row with room to its side. On a phone there rarely is, so it opens above or below instead.

states.title: Closed, open, and how it closes
states.description: A press on the trigger opens it; there's no hover, focus, or timer. While it's open a clear layer covers the page: the next press anywhere, Escape on the web, or Android's back button closes it. After Escape, focus stays on the trigger. The screen can also open it itself with open and hear every close through onOpenChange.
blocks: Press the i to open it; press anywhere to close it.

sizing.title: Hugs short text, wraps at 280 px
sizing.description: The bubble is as wide as its text up to 280 px, then wraps; padding is 12 × 8 px and text 14 px on 18 px lines. A width on the content sets it instead, like Figma's Custom Width variant.
blocks: One line: the bubble hugs it.
Wraps at 280 px. Two or three lines is the most people will read.
A set width of 200 px, Figma's Custom Width On: the same text wraps sooner.

content.title: One plain explanation
content.description: Explain one term in a sentence or two of plain text, and keep the term itself on the page. Plain text and Coin Text both get the white label style. A press inside it just closes it, so never put an action there.

sources.title: Use the public Tooltip contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78, built from Biscuit’s main at dbe0e02 (27 October) and taken from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Tooltip is a near-black bubble with a downward arrow near its bottom left or right, in two variants, Custom Width Off (up to 280 px) and On. In code the bubble hugs its text up to 280 px or takes a set width, centres the arrow on the trigger, offers 12 placements, and stays 8 px inside the screen. It opens on press only, over the whole window, and the next press anywhere closes it. It measures its text each time it opens, so a bubble whose text has grown still sits clear of its trigger. On the web the bubble is a tooltip tied to its trigger, and Escape closes it. Storybook’s stories use a plain grey box as the trigger; these examples pass a Coin IconButton with asChild, though a Coin button nested inside the trigger opens it too.
